learningObjectives: Apply the core Attribute structure and reuse-via-Class principles across multiple TestSheets.
Structure Agile acceptance criteria using the Given-When-Then pattern inside a TestSheet.
Build a TestSheet's structure externally (Notepad/Excel) and import it with Create Element Structure from Clipboard.
Apply independent readability and risk-based maintenance guidance alongside documented Tosca reuse and import procedures.

elements.description: Use a centrally managed Class for repeated Attribute structures. Unresolved references share changes in both directions: editing the reference also changes the Class. Resolve a reference before making a consumer-specific change; other consumers can remain shared. Decide on reuse from actual maintenance needs, not a mandatory two-use threshold.

Independent Quilyn layout: Administration for non-business data, Precondition for setup, Process for actions and Verification for expected results. This four-group skeleton is one modeling choice, not a documented requirement for every TestSheet. Match the hierarchy and relevance to the test objective.

A template for writing acceptance tests for user stories, useful when TestCase Design needs to reflect an Agile way of working. An acceptance test built this way has three parts: Given (the context and preconditions), When (the action being carried out), Then (the observable, expected outcome).

Independent example: Given a returning customer is logged in and has a saved shipping address, When the customer opens checkout, Then the saved address is displayed for confirmation. Keep the observable address result separate from a later order-submission action; each assertion should state the behavior being tested.

elements.text: In this optional layout, Given maps to Precondition, When to Process and Then to Verification. This is a conceptual mapping; Tosca does not automatically execute Gherkin merely because those Attribute names are used.

bulletPoints: Given states context, When states an action or event, Then states an observable result; Attribute naming is independent of executable step bindings.

elements.description: For a large or complex TestSheet, it can be faster to sketch the Attribute hierarchy in Notepad or Excel first, then import it in one shot, instead of creating each Attribute by hand inside Tosca.

elements.title: Documented import workflow
items: Prepare and copy a structure in an external program such as Excel or Notepad.
Right-click the target TestSheet and select Create Element Structure from Clipboard from the mini toolbar.
Inspect the resulting hierarchy and rearrange it where needed. The accessed article does not specify a universal tab/column indentation grammar; do not treat an untested layout as guaranteed.

elements.text: Try a small sample before importing a large hierarchy. Clipboard import creates structure; verify the data, combinations and template mapping separately.

bulletPoints: Use the documented clipboard command and inspect the imported hierarchy; specific indentation formats need validation in your installed version.

elements.title: Independent Quilyn maintenance checklist
items: Name scenarios and Attributes in clear business language; keep technical binding details in the automation layer.
Use Character and Position markers according to the intended scenario, not as decorative labels.
Group long lists by meaningful business concepts without deleting relevant choices. No universal six-to-eight-item threshold is established by the accessed docs.
Create reusable Classes where shared maintenance is useful; inspect references before edits or deletion.
Specify observable expected outcomes and trace design scope back to relevant Requirements.
Select a coverage method and constraints deliberately rather than equating fewer rows with sufficient coverage.
Inspect imported structure and template mapping before instantiating executable TestCases.
Keep boundary cases in recurring regression where range, validation or integration risk warrants them; do not discard them solely because they ran once.

elements.text: Independent exercise: compare two TestSheets for repeated data, introduce a Class where sharing is useful, resolve one reference for a consumer-specific change, and import a small hierarchy using the documented command. Academy videos/exercise files require access and are not certified here.

examPitfalls.title: Turning every Attribute structure into a Class
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Converting a one-off Attribute structure into a Class 'just in case' it might be reused later.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use shared Classes where centralized maintenance is justified. A fixed two-use threshold is not established by the accessed documentation; consider reference coupling and consumer-specific changes.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming clipboard formatting without inspecting the result
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Importing a large structure using an unverified indentation convention and assuming the hierarchy is correct.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Start with a small sample, use Create Element Structure from Clipboard, and inspect/rearrange the hierarchy. The accessed documentation names Excel and Notepad but does not specify a universal indentation grammar.

examPitfalls.title: Writing Attributes in technical, Module/TestStep language
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Naming Attributes after technical implementation details (e.g. field IDs, control names) instead of business meaning.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Attributes should be described in business language, so anyone reading the TestSheet — not just automation engineers — understands what's being tested.

examPitfalls.title: Discarding boundary cases from regression automatically
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming boundary behavior cannot regress because it passed in a previous release.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Retain boundary coverage according to change and failure risk. Range, validation and integration changes can make previously passing boundary scenarios fail again.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An Attribute structure is used in exactly one TestSheet and there are no plans to reuse it elsewhere. Should it be converted into a Class?

options.text: Yes, always — Classes are always the safer choice.
Not solely for reuse: consider the maintenance benefit and shared-reference coupling before converting a one-off structure.
Only if it has more than 6 Attributes.
Only if it contains Boundary Instances.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about when the extra indirection of a Class actually pays off.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Classes centrally manage repeated data. For a one-off structure with no reuse plan, there is no automatic benefit from sharing; the accessed docs do not establish a mandatory two-use rule.

optionExplanations.A: Shared references introduce coupling; a Class is not always the safest choice for one-off data.
optionExplanations.B: This evaluates the actual reuse and maintenance need instead of applying an invented threshold.
optionExplanations.C: Attribute count alone does not determine whether the structure should be shared.
optionExplanations.D: Boundary values do not by themselves require a reusable Class.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester has copied a proposed Attribute structure from Excel. Which documented operation imports it into an existing TestSheet?

options.text: Right-click the TestSheet and select Create Element Structure from Clipboard.
Excel structures cannot be imported into Tosca.

practiceQuiz.hint: Look for the command that imports a copied element hierarchy.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The TestSheets article documents Create Element Structure from Clipboard on the target TestSheet mini toolbar. Inspect and rearrange the imported structure as needed.

optionExplanations.A: Arrange Instances organizes existing Instances rather than importing an element hierarchy.
optionExplanations.B: This is the documented TestSheet command for a structure copied from an external program.
optionExplanations.C: This Requirements command replaces planned substitutes with physical TestCase links.
optionExplanations.D: The documentation explicitly supports preparing a structure in Excel or Notepad.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the independent Precondition / Process / Verification layout, which Given-When-Then part expresses the Precondition?

options.text: None — Given-When-Then doesn't map to the core Attribute structure.

practiceQuiz.hint: Precondition describes the setup state needed before the action happens.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Given establishes the initial context, so it maps conceptually to Precondition. When is the action and Then is the expected observable result. Attribute names do not create executable Gherkin bindings.

optionExplanations.A: Given describes the initial context required before the action.
optionExplanations.B: When expresses the action or event, mapped here to Process.
optionExplanations.C: Then expresses the expected observable outcome, mapped here to Verification.
optionExplanations.D: There is a conceptual mapping in this layout, although it is not an automatic runtime binding.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An Attribute has 14 child items and reviewers find its flat list difficult to understand. Which independent maintainability improvement preserves the relevant test data?

options.text: Nothing — flat lists of any size are fine.
Group the items under meaningful sub-Attributes and check that the test intent remains clear.
Convert all 14 items into a single Value Attribute.

practiceQuiz.hint: Improve the hierarchy without discarding relevant choices.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Meaningful grouping can improve readability without deleting coverage. Tosca supports nested Attributes; a universal six-to-eight-item vendor limit was not established by the accessed articles.

optionExplanations.A: The scenario states that the current layout is difficult to understand; leaving it unchanged does not address that issue.
optionExplanations.B: Grouping by meaning improves readability while preserving the distinct relevant choices.
optionExplanations.C: Collapsing distinct choices into one value loses their intended structure and meaning.
optionExplanations.D: Deleting relevant test data to meet an arbitrary count can remove needed coverage.

quickRecap.value: Use Classes for useful shared maintenance; unresolved reference edits affect the source Class too.
Given → Precondition, When → Process, Then → Verification.
Copy external structure, use Create Element Structure from Clipboard, then inspect the imported hierarchy.
Business language, not technical Module/TestStep language; names should state the test focus.
Group by meaningful concepts; no universal six-to-eight-item limit is certified here.
Retain recurring boundary coverage according to regression risk, not an automatic one-time rule.
